title: W sklepie · zwroty
title_en: At the shop · what to say
note: Situations/chunk unit — what Dad actually says in a Polish shop. Fixed phrases, learned whole, no rule slides. NEW words taught here: ile, kosztuje, poprosze, place, karta(inst), gotowka(inst), tylko, ogladac/ogladam. INSTRUMENTAL QUARANTINE (2026-08-05): 'Place karta.' / 'Place gotowka.' are taught STRICTLY as frozen blocks. The case is never named, never explained, never contrasted, and no instrumental structure id is tagged. a2_inst_z is a later unit and owns that ground. Every quiz choice touching these phrases is a WHOLE PHRASE, never a four-way ending drill (karta/karte/karty/karta) — that would open the case by the back door. 'Czy moge zaplacic karta?' from the brief was changed to 'Czy moge placic karta?': zaplacic is PERFECTIVE and the standing decision for this batch is imperfective-only, even in fixed chunks. The imperfective version is genuine shop Polish and keeps moge + infinitive (can_inf). 'Poprosze' is kept despite being formally perfective — it is on James's target list and in the tree note, it is opaque to the learner, and it is presented as an unanalysable politeness word: never conjugated, never glossed as a verb form, no aspect or future content attached to it. Real contrast the unit DOES teach, because both cases are already taught: Poprosze kawe (Accusative, same form as after mam) vs Czy jest kawa? (Nominative, plain dictionary form). The conjunction 'i' is deliberately absent — it is not in POOL (see report).

intro.title: Poproszę — the word that does most of the work
intro.body:
In a Polish shop you almost never need a full sentence. Poproszę is the polite "I'll have… / …please". Put it in front of the thing you want and you are finished.

One thing to watch, and you already know it. Whatever follows Poproszę takes the same form it takes after mam. Mam kawę → Poproszę kawę. That is the accusative, and for most masculine and neuter words it changes nothing at all: chleb, ser, cukier, mleko, paragon all stay exactly as they are.

Poproszę itself never changes. Treat it as one polite word, not as a verb to be conjugated.
intro.body_pl: Poproszę kawę. Poproszę chleb. Poproszę paragon.

rows: kawa → kawę, the same -ę as in mam kawę
ask for this at the till

intro.title: Ile to kosztuje? · Czy jest…? — the two questions you will use most
intro.body:
Ile means "how much / how many". You have been saying it since the very first weeks — Ile masz lat? Same word, new job.

Ile to kosztuje? = "How much does this cost?" To means "this", so point at the thing while you say it. If you would rather name the thing, put its name where to was: Ile kosztuje kawa?

Czy jest…? is how you ask whether the shop has something. After both Ile kosztuje and Czy jest the noun stays in its plain dictionary form — kawa, chleb, mleko. So the two frames of this unit pull in opposite directions, and it is worth ten seconds: Poproszę kawę, but Czy jest kawa?
intro.body_pl: Ile to kosztuje? Ile kosztuje kawa? Czy jest chleb?

rows: How much does the coffee cost?
Is there any bread? / Do you have bread?
kawę — this frame is the odd one out

examples.en: How much does the book cost?
Excuse me, is there any sugar?

intro.title: Paying — take these whole
intro.body:
Płacę kartą = "I'm paying by card." Płacę gotówką = "I'm paying cash."

These two are fixed phrases and this unit asks you to learn them exactly as they stand. Do not change the last word, and do not try to build the phrases out of karta and gotówka — the endings on them belong to something you meet properly in a later unit. Say the phrase whole and it is always right.

Czy mogę płacić kartą? is the polite version: "Can I pay by card?" That one you can take apart — it is mogę plus a plain infinitive, the same shape as mogę czytać.

Kasa is the till, the checkout. Gdzie jest kasa? finds it.
intro.body_pl: Płacę kartą. Płacę gotówką. Czy mogę płacić kartą? Gdzie jest kasa?

rows: mogę + infinitive, as in mogę czytać
the last thing you say at the till

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the till?
That's everything. I'm paying by card.
Excuse me. Can I pay by card?

intro.title: Browsing, and getting out politely
intro.body:
Two more, and the shop is survivable.

Tylko means "only, just". On its own with words you already have: Tylko kawa, dziękuję — "Just a coffee, thanks."

Oglądam means "I'm looking (at things), I'm browsing". It is an -am verb, exactly like mam and czytam, so there is no new pattern in it.

Put the two together and you get Tylko oglądam — the standard answer when an assistant offers to help and you would rather be left alone.

To wszystko, dziękuję = "That's everything, thank you." Every word in it is already yours. Say it at the till when the assistant is waiting to see if you want anything else.
intro.body_pl: Tylko kawa, dziękuję. Tylko oglądam. To wszystko, dziękuję.

examples.en: Good day. A cheese, please. That's everything, thank you.
examples.pl: Dzień dobry. Poproszę ser. To wszystko, dziękuję.

examples.en: A soup, please. I'm paying cash.

quiz.explain: Ile is the same word you already use in Ile masz lat? — it means how much or how many. Here it is doing the price job.

quiz.prompt: You want a coffee. You say:
quiz.explain: Czy jest kawa? only asks whether they have any. Poproszę is what actually orders it.
Poproszę takes the accusative, the same form you already use after mam: mam kawę → poproszę kawę.

quiz.prompt: Is there any coffee? →  Czy jest ___?
quiz.explain: Czy jest asks whether the thing exists at all, so the noun stays in its plain dictionary form — the nominative. This is the frame that does NOT behave like Poproszę.

quiz.explain: Karta is a card, gotówka is cash. Learn each phrase as one block and you never have to think about the ending.

Czy jest kasa? would ask whether the shop has a till at all. Gdzie asks where it is.

quiz.prompt: You have finished and the assistant is waiting. You say:

quiz.explain: Mogę is always followed by the plain infinitive — płacić, not płacę. It is the same shape as mogę czytać.
A czy question is a yes/no question, so the answer comes back with tak or nie, not with another request.

type_items.explain: To means this — you are pointing at the thing. Swap in a name and you get Ile kosztuje kawa?
Poproszę takes the accusative, the form you already use after mam: mam kawę.
Chleb is masculine and not alive, so the accusative looks identical to the dictionary form. Nothing to add.
After Czy jest the noun keeps its plain dictionary form. Compare Poproszę cukier — here it happens to look the same, because cukier is masculine.
This is a fixed phrase. Learn the two words as one block and leave the ending alone — it belongs to a pattern you meet later.
Same fixed phrase, different means of payment. Take it whole, exactly as it stands.
Mogę is followed by the infinitive płacić — never by płacę. Czy at the front simply turns it into a question.

Items 6-7 still type Płacę kartą / Płacę gotówką whole, so the frozen phrase itself is still produced.

type_items.explain: Oglądam sits in the -am family with mam and czytam, so the ending is one you can already build.
